items.text: Finley (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so visit claims can be checked against the nest changes without guesswork.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eagles

items.text: Alex (would change): Make the dawn reports more explicit about who visited whom, so players can check claims without guessing about egg rules.
items.title: 20261113-015201-meowfia-v8-s501

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make the dawn reports state the exact rule that produced each egg, such as "target visited no one", so players can check claims without arguing over the wording.
items.title: 20261113-015201-meowfia-v8-s501

items.text: Casey (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can check claims without reconstructing every night from egg counts.
items.title: 20261113-015201-meowfia-v8-s501

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make the dawn reports name who visited you when an egg changes, so the table can check claims without guessing.
items.title: 20261113-015201-meowfia-v8-s501

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the dawn reports say who visited you when the animal's egg depends on visitors, so players can check claims more easily.
items.title: 20261113-015201-meowfia-v8-s501

items.text: Finley (would change): Publish each player's visit and egg changes in one shared, checkable log so bluffing about egg counts is easier to catch.
items.title: 20261113-015201-meowfia-v8-s501

items.text: Runaway lead: Finley banked 36 points in round 1 from a single Farm kill, and 3 rounds are too few to recover. Consider a lower multiplier or a cap on Meowfia stakes.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Players often threw nothing or low cards at an already doomed target, such as Finley in round 2. This makes the vote less costly than it should be. Consider a minimum throw or a penalty for throwing nothing.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Alex (would change): Have the dawn report name each visitor, so players can check claims against their own egg counts instead of inferring them.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players don't have to reconstruct each other's egg math.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Casey (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about which visits caused which hugs or eggs, so players can check each other's claims without guessing.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Drew (would change): Make the egg-gain wording for each animal explicit in the dawn report or rules so players are not arguing about who gains from whom.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Ellis (would change): Show each player's throw total as a running tally or reveal the throws more clearly, since nobody could see the values and it made the vote-counting feel opaque.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make each animal's gain rule restated in the dawn report, so players argue about claims rather than the rules. I would also show visit directions explicitly in the day summary.
items.title: Finley's Quiet Harvest

items.text: Runaway leader: Finley banked a 13 and ended at 30 against 16. A single King throw decides the whole game. Cap banked value per throw or add a catch-up rule.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: A Wink on the first beat leaves no counterplay. The target loses their speech but keeps their throw, and here that throw was worth 13. Dead players' throws should be reduced, or the Wink should cost something.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: Hugged players are not told they were hugged. Their results look real and they defend the cat in good faith. That may be intended, but it made round 2 close to unsolvable for Farm.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: Tie rule: Farm vs Meowfia at 4–4 eggsecuted the Farm player. Together with the fact that votes are cards, this rewards Meowfia for spreading votes. Consider favoring neither side or re-voting.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: Alex (would change): I'd make nest changes from each visit easier to check, for example by listing who visited whom at dawn. Right now players have to infer visits from egg counts, which invites confusion and bluffing.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: Blair (would change): Make the dawn reports and visitor information clearer, so players can check claims without guessing which rule applies to which role.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: Drew (would change): Make the night target requirement clearer on the prompt for every role, and show each player's visit target in the dawn report so no one has to guess what happened.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make the Storyteller state the tie-break outcome more clearly, or explain it in the rules, since a 4-4 tie decided round 2 and was easy to miss.
items.title: The Thirteen-Egg Snipe

items.text: One round decided the game. Round 2 gave the winning cats 16 points each, and Farm rounds paid at most 12, so the lead was unassailable. Consider capping the 2x bonus or raising the Farm payout.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Farm players threw Wilds and tiny stakes in round 1, so the game was low-stakes. Banking Farm stakes only when right invites the same timid play.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Two players died as Meowfia in rounds 1 and 3 and finished with 7 points. Losing teams feel out of the game early, so catch-up may be needed.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make the dawn reports include the visitor's role, so players could check claims against each other more easily.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Blair (would change): Have dawn reports name the visitor's role or the visit direction, so hugs and visit claims are easier to check.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Casey (would change): I would make the dawn reports more explicit about who visited whom, so players can cross-check claims without guessing at contradictions.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Drew (would change): I'd make the dawn reports show who visited whom, so visit claims can be checked instead of argued over.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Ellis (would change): Make visit directions and hug results appear in the public day summary, so players don't have to reconstruct who visited whom from conflicting claims.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make dawn reports name the visitor and the visited player explicitly, so everyone can check claims against the same facts.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: Blair, round 3: Got the visit direction between Blair and Finley backwards, then corrected it.
items.title: Snowball of the Cats

items.text: The scoring snowballs. A round-1 banked 8 plus a solo cat win left Ellis far ahead, and nobody changed their play against the leader. Fix: reduce rewards for dead players or tie-break against the leader.
items.title: The Lone Cat Wins

items.text: Players barely acted on the standings. Despite the rules' stress on outscoring teammates, throws followed the consensus every round, and the leader was never targeted.
items.title: The Lone Cat Wins

items.text: Votes converged on one target almost at once in every round, so the vote was rarely in doubt. Wild and low-card throws cost nothing, which also removes risk. Fix: make small throws cost something.
items.title: The Lone Cat Wins

items.text: Blair (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about what a confused player can and cannot trust, so players aren't stuck guessing which claims hold.
items.title: The Lone Cat Wins

items.text: Casey (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about visitors, since many claims were built on unverifiable or confused reports. Clearer reports would make the deduction less about guessing who was lying.
items.title: The Lone Cat Wins

items.text: Ellis (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about which eggs come from which visitor, since several players' stories hinged on it.
items.title: The Lone Cat Wins

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make dawn reports name the players who visited, not just the animals. That would make the night deductions much clearer.
items.title: The Lone Cat Wins

items.text: Big early banks decide the game. Casey's 23 points in round 1 and Drew's 31 total left Alex and Ellis out of contention, so later rounds feel meaningless for them. Consider capping banked values or catching up the trailing players.
items.title: Winks and Wild Cards

items.text: Dead players keep throwing, and the Wink's anonymity plus a free kill makes Meowfia too strong. Blair winked in two rounds with no real cost.
items.title: Winks and Wild Cards

items.text: Meowfia who stay silent (Blair in round 2) are never pressed. Add a rule that forces claims.
items.title: Winks and Wild Cards

items.text: Scores are announced but the standings barely affected play. Few players chased the leader, since everyone voted the same way.
items.title: Winks and Wild Cards

items.text: Alex (would change): Put the visitor list in every dawn report for visit-based roles, so claims like "two visitors" can be checked instead of argued.
items.title: Winks and Wild Cards

items.text: Finley (would change): Show each player the exact visitor list in their dawn report, so visit claims can be checked without argument.
items.title: Winks and Wild Cards

items.text: Casey, round 1: Claimed Drew and Finley visited her. In fact they visited Blair, and Casey's own report listed them as Blair's visitors.
items.title: Winks and Wild Cards

items.text: Snowballing: Ellis's single 14-point bank in round 2 made the final round nearly meaningless. Nobody else could catch him. Consider capping banked points or giving catch-up value to losers.
items.title: The Wild Banker

items.text: Players throw Wilds and low cards at consensus targets, so winners earn tiny scores (0 to 3). Only high throws matter, and the table rarely makes them. Raise the reward for low throws or lower the King payoff.
items.title: The Wild Banker

items.text: Blair (would change): Make the dawn reports and role text clearer about whether an egg goes to the visitor or the visited player, so the table doesn't argue over rules.
items.title: The Wild Banker

items.text: Drew (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited a player and whether a role was blocked or confused, so claims can be checked more easily.
items.title: The Wild Banker

items.text: Ellis (would change): Make the dawn reports less ambiguous about who an egg came from, so players can check claims without a long rules debate.
items.title: The Wild Banker

items.text: Finley, round 2: Said his -2 came from a confused report and then treated it as noise. Confusion changes only the report, and the cards still had to be discarded.
items.title: The Wild Banker

items.text: Alex banked huge cards early (12 and 25 points) and the leader was never pressured. The gap made rounds 3 irrelevant for the win. Fix: cap banked value or make high throws riskier.
items.title: Alex Runs Away

items.text: Nobody tried to win the game against Alex. Everyone only fought for their own round, so the table never used the standings. Rounds felt like the same vote.
items.title: Alex Runs Away

items.text: Alex (would change): Make dawn reports say who visited you, not just how many eggs came in, so claims like Blair's Drew visit can be checked directly.
items.title: Alex Runs Away

items.text: Casey (would change): Tell each Meowfia player who their teammates are at the start of a Meowfia round, so a team can coordinate instead of throwing at each other.
items.title: Alex Runs Away

items.text: Drew (would change): Show each player's visit target publicly at dawn, so day claims about who visited whom can be checked directly.
items.title: Alex Runs Away

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make it clearer when a visit is recorded and who visited whom, so claims are easier to check. Some dawn reports were hard to follow.
items.title: Alex Runs Away

items.text: Finley, round 1: Said Alex's story about his visit was wrong, although Alex only reported seeing Finley visit Blair.
items.title: Alex Runs Away

items.text: Scores favored the lucky: Drew won with two Meowfia rounds while the player on the wrong side of two misreads sat at 7. Little late comeback was possible, so the final round felt flat.
items.title: Eggs Nobody Could Source

items.text: Runaway leader: banking 9 or 17 in one throw dwarfs the 0-4 swings elsewhere. Alex won with 29 against 12. Fix: cap the value banked per round or throw size.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Winning a round is almost a coin flip for the thrower, but high-card banking rewards the best positioned player the most. The three-round format leaves no comeback after round 1 ends 3-4 points apiece.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Players claimed roles that switch round to round and treated the switch as a lie. They also ignored that roles are re-dealt, so cross-round claims were noise. Meanwhile, Wilds were thrown at no cost, so throws signal little.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Alex (would change): Make dawn reports name the players who visited you, not only the animals, so every claim can be checked against the same facts.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Blair (would change): Make dawn reports say who visited you when an egg is gained, so a +1 or +0 can be checked against claims instead of guessed at.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Casey (would change): Have dawn reports name the visiting players and animals, so claims can be checked against actual visits.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the role reveals and egg-source explanations clearer at dawn, so players can check claims without guessing which visit caused which egg.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Finley (would change): Make the dawn reports say who visited you, not just the egg count, so players can check claims against each other.
items.title: Wink, Wilds, Runaway Leader

items.text: Unexplained eggs, like Casey's +1, cannot be traced and get treated as proof of guilt. Consider telling a player their egg count came from a visit, or limiting these effects.
items.title: Three Wrong Eggsecutions

items.text: Throwing a cheap card at the winning side's target pays out the full value of the winner's best throw. Blair banked 8 with two 4s, which is a runaway lead, and the bank rewards a Meowfia win far more than a Farm win.
items.title: Three Wrong Eggsecutions

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make the dawn reports more explicit about who visited whom, since much of the day went to guessing whose story was true.
items.title: Three Wrong Eggsecutions

items.text: Drew (would change): I'd make the dawn reports for confused players clearer about which parts are wrong, so a confused player can still reason from their own result.
items.title: Three Wrong Eggsecutions

items.text: Ellis (would change): I would make the dawn reports and visit logs more explicit, such as stating exactly which visitors counted toward each egg change, so claims could be checked.
items.title: Three Wrong Eggsecutions

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players don't argue over whether a visit counts for the target or the actor.
items.title: Three Wrong Eggsecutions

items.text: Everyone visits the score leader or the same person, so night info is redundant. Round 2 had five visits to Alex and round 3 had five to Ellis. Consider hiding the leader or limiting visits per target.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Scoring snowballs. Winning a round with high cards produces 15 points, which swamps the rest, so round 3 decided the game. Cap banked values or add a catch-up rule.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Alex (would change): I'd make dawn reports list who visited you when a role depends on visitors, so claims could be checked directly.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Blair (would change): Show each player who visited them, not just the count change, so claims can be checked directly.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Casey (would change): Make the dawn report show who visited you when the role's rules say you learn it, so players can check claims directly instead of inferring them from egg counts.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Drew (would change): Have dawn reports name who visited you, or at least show it when an egg is gained, so the day can check claims directly.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Ellis (would change): Make the dawn report state plainly who visited you and whether a visit was blocked, so players don't have to guess what their own nest changes mean.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Finley (would change): Make dawn reports clearer about who visited you and whether a visit paid anything, so players can check claims without guessing.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Finley, round 3: Did not see that the hug on Ellis explained his own zero, and treated it as proof against Ellis.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Casey, round 3: Did not weigh the hug on Ellis, and doubted Alex's confirmed list.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Drew, round 2: Said Blair and Casey changed roles between rounds as evidence, forgetting roles are re-dealt.
items.title: Four Visitors, One Wink

items.text: Confusion and hugs look like lies. Ellis's confused report and the round 1 hug were treated as contradictions. Fix: make the confusion effect clearer, or give a way to confirm it.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Round 3 had only one Meowfia and no one else to contest the vote, so Farm bandwagoned on a weak case. Fix: add something to draw doubt, or require more than a lost egg count as evidence.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Scoring was lopsided. Finley led from round 1 and was never pressured, and a Farm loss still let him keep 23. Fix: add leader-catch-up pressure or a bigger swing for round 3.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make the dawn reports show who visited whom, or at least state which egg came from which visit, so players can check claims without guessing.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make it clearer in the dawn report which visitor or animal produced each egg, so players don't have to guess from counts.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Casey (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about who gained or lost eggs from which visit, so players can check each other's claims without guesswork.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the dawn reports say which egg source each gain came from, so players don't have to reverse-engineer every count during the day.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about who gained eggs from which visit, so players can verify egg counts without guessing at card mechanics.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Ellis, round 3: Said someone visited him, though only Finley did.
items.title: The Wink Spoils Finley

items.text: Round 1 had no information. Every nest stayed at 5, and the vote was a coin flip that killed a Farm player. Fix: guarantee some night effect, or give a role that always shows a result.
items.title: The Wink Gives It Away

items.text: The standings barely mattered. Players mostly threw low cards and all voted together, so the 'outscore your teammates' tension never appeared. Fix: make throws costlier or high cards more tempting.
items.title: The Wink Gives It Away

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make night results and visit counts clearer in the dawn reports, so players can check each other's claims without having to work out role mechanics.
items.title: The Wink Gives It Away

items.text: Casey, round 2: Claimed Drew's 'nobody visited me' was false because visitors gained eggs. Visitors did visit Drew, and Drew's claim was actually wrong in a different way.
items.title: The Wink Gives It Away

items.text: Vote pile-ons were near unanimous in every round, so bandwagons beat deduction. Few players held out or checked a claim against nest sizes.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: Winning a round pays far too much for one high-card throw (Blair 14, Alex 15). That decided first place and made the other rounds nearly irrelevant. Cap what a round can bank, or limit the throw size.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: Lone Meowfia don't know each other, so a single Meowfia with a Wink faces no real risk. Consider a cost or tell for Wink use.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: Alex (would change): Let dawn reports name the actual visitors, so players could check each other's counts instead of guessing from nest sizes.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: Blair (would change): Show each player's visit list and visitor count in the dawn reports, so claims can be checked without guessing about the rules.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: Casey (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who is confused, since "your report may be wrong" made honest players like Drew hard to trust or clear.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: Drew (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about whether a visit actually happened, so players don't spend the day arguing over counts that a confused report has already muddied.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: Drew, round 1: Drew, Alex and Finley all counted Blair's own visit as a second visitor, then voted on that reading.
items.title: The Wink Lands Late

items.text: The leader ran away. Drew banked 16 in round 1 and 21 in round 3. High cards thrown on the winning side score full value, so rich nests snowball. Cap banked value per round, or reduce the Kings' value.
items.title: Two Farm Casualties

items.text: Meowfia won two rounds by eggsecuting the same wrongly accused Farm player. Mixed claims and no reliable verification made Farm vote on noise. Give Farm a stronger source of verified information.
items.title: Two Farm Casualties

items.text: Players had no memory pressure across rounds. Alex and Casey were attacked for claiming different roles in different rounds, even though roles are re-dealt. Remind players of this, or hide previous-round roles.
items.title: Two Farm Casualties

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the dawn egg reports and role claims easier to check against each other, so a claim like "my nest went up by 2" can be verified against the visits listed.
items.title: Two Farm Casualties

items.text: Farm won all three rounds and the Meowfia never threatened. Cats do not know each other and cannot act on the table. Consider giving them a team-wide night signal, or a stronger Wink-like tool.
items.title: The Hawk's Egg

items.text: Finley's 25-point banked throw decided the game by round 2. Big King throws on a sure vote snowball. Consider capping banked value per round or scaling it so a leader cannot run away.
items.title: The Hawk's Egg

items.text: Alex (would change): I'd make dawn reports clearer about which visit produced which egg change, so players can cross-check claims without guessing.
items.title: The Hawk's Egg

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make dawn reports say outright which claims they can verify, so players don't waste turns arguing over whether a count is confused or real.
items.title: The Hawk's Egg

items.text: Casey (would change): I'd make the role-to-visit results clearer to the table, so players can check each other's claims more easily.
items.title: The Hawk's Egg

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make dawn reports say which visit caused a confused result, so players can judge role claims more easily.
items.title: The Hawk's Egg

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make it clearer when a player is dead and whether their throws still count, since that was easy to misread mid-vote.
items.title: The Hawk's Egg

items.text: Farm eggsecuted a Farm player all three rounds. Evidence was too weak for deduction, so the vote was driven by who sounded off, not by who was lying.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Silence paid off. Finley said nothing for most of rounds 1 and 3 and won. Farm players had no reason to press a quiet player, so consider a reward for speaking or a penalty for staying silent.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Hug 'no effect at tier 60' lines in the log are confusing and no player was told about them. Casey and Ellis did not know a hug had landed.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Scores were top-heavy. Casey's one round-2 win made the last round close to irrelevant, which hurts tension. The banked-card value is too swingy compared with kept cards.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Alex (would change): I'd make the dawn reports show which visitor and which target each claim relates to, so players can check claims without guessing at role rules.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Blair (would change): Publish each player's visit and egg change on the day list, so the claims can be checked without relying on memory and wording.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Drew (would change): Give the table a way to verify claims, such as showing each player's visit list to the others, so people aren't left guessing whose report is wrong.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the dawn reports say who visited you when the role is a visit-based one, so players don't have to reconstruct it from egg counts.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make the animal texts explicit about whether a role's own visit counts and where each egg lands, so players aren't guessing at the rules mid-day.
items.title: Silent Floofer Wins Twice

items.text: Votes pile on one target fast. In rounds 2 and 3 five players threw at the same Meowfia with no real doubt. Consider fewer clear tells or scarcer information.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Meowfia winning round 1 scored nothing for Finley, since a Wild was thrown. Winning as Meowfia depends on throwing real cards, and nobody wants to.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Players threw Wilds and low cards almost every time, so the score race was decided by who happened to be on the winning team. Ellis's lead came from one +5 and +7 banked. Consider making thrown value matter more.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Alex (would change): Make role claims and visit results easier to verify, perhaps by having the Storyteller confirm each visit's effect publicly.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Casey (confused by): Roles and claims reshuffle every round, so a player's earlier claim is easy to misread, and confused reports make egg counts unreliable. I could not tell which dawn reports to trust.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Casey (would change): Make the Storyteller's dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so the table can verify claims without relying on guesswork.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Drew (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so claims are easier to check without guessing.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make it clearer when a dawn report is confused, such as showing which parts of it are wrong. That would reduce wasted suspicion on honest players.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Ellis, round 1: Said Alex claimed Ellis visited him, when Alex said Ellis visited Blair.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Casey, round 2: Said Blair's confusion proved Blair wrong about Casey, though Blair's own confused report was the unreliable part.
items.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes

items.text: Ellis ran away with the game. He won all three rounds and threw 19, 15 and 15 points of cards while dead or alive. With 37 points after round 2, nobody could catch him. Consider a cap on points per round, or a catch-up rule for the leader, because the final round had no stakes.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: The 'only first place wins' rule did not shape play. Nobody tried to stop Ellis or throw at him. His teammates and opponents all helped him bank points. Players needed some way to hurt the leader.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: Winking the loudest accuser hands Meowfia's identity to the table. It happened twice, and both Wink users were voted out the same day. Make the Wink harder to trace, or make it less obvious who had the means.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: The dead can still throw their highest cards and bank them with no risk. Ellis banked 19 points in round 1 after he was dead. A dead player should throw fewer cards, or at lower value.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since confused reports and mismatched egg counts made the day discussion hard to pin down.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make it clearer when a Wink is used and who holds one, since silent collapses were hard to read.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: Ellis (would change): I would make the dawn reports spell out who gained or lost eggs and why, so players can check visit claims without mixing up roles.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: Blair, round 2: Said Casey was 'out this round'. Casey was alive and had visited her.
items.title: The Ellis Runaway

items.text: Round 1 was a quick pile-on. A lone Meowfia with a bad bluff gets killed by beat 3. Fix: give the lone Meowfia more cover or role information.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: The winning team's banked cards swing the whole game. Round 3 gave Blair 13 and Casey 17 and ended the contest. Fix: cap banked points or reduce how much high cards matter.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Dead Farm players like Drew and Finley lose all voice, and the Wink has no real counter. Fix: give Farm some way to detect or answer winks.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Early rounds are mostly random visits with no information. Players mostly said the same things and then said nothing. Fix: reward unique information or give them a reason to commit to a target.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Players dodged the role question for several beats (Ellis, Blair) and the table could not act on it. Fix: make refusing to claim costly, or have the app prompt the claim.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Blair (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about who is confused, so players can tell which parts of a claim to trust. I would also make it clear which player's secret role is hidden from teammates.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Casey (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about confusion, so players can tell when an egg count or visit claim is unreliable.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Drew (would change): I'd make the Storyteller reveal each player's confusion status or visit results more clearly, so Farm players can separate a wrong report from a lying one.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Ellis (would change): I would make the dawn egg reports and confusion notices clearer, so players can check each other's claims without guessing which reports were wrong.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Finley (would change): I would have dawn reports say which visitor gave each egg, so public claims about egg gains are easier to verify.
items.title: Wink Wins Round Three

items.text: Round 1 had too little information. With no checkable witnesses, the vote was just a guess. Fix: give every Farm role a small guaranteed clue.
items.title: Wink Wins Rounds

items.text: Score snowballing: Blair's 14-point win in round 2 made him nearly unreachable. Fix: cap the cards banked per round, or add catch-up.
items.title: Wink Wins Rounds

items.text: Dead players still throwing cards and scoring is odd. Blair and Drew banked points after death, and the day's beat structure left Ellis with little to do after the vote.
items.title: Wink Wins Rounds

items.text: Alex (would change): Include a short reminder of each animal's nest-change rule in the dawn report, so players don't misremember them mid-day.
items.title: Wink Wins Rounds

items.text: Casey (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which rule caused each egg change, so players aren't left guessing who gained what from whom.
items.title: Wink Wins Rounds

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd have dawn reports say explicitly which rule produced each egg gained or lost, so players can check claims without re-deriving the mechanics mid-vote.
items.title: Wink Wins Rounds

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make the dawn reports show each visitor's role, so players can check claims against actual egg changes rather than arguing from memory.
items.title: Wink Wins Rounds

items.text: The table herds onto one target. Every round had 5 or 6 throws at one player and little doubt. Consider rewards for splitting votes or a visible vote tally before throwing.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Drew was Farm and eggsecuted every round, scoring nearly nothing. Early errors snowball, and a player being right is rarely rewarded. Add a comeback mechanic.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Cards were mostly thrown at low value, and the scoring rarely felt like a decision. Round 2 gave Ellis 0 points for a win because only thrown cards score. Meowfia winners who throw nothing valuable gain nothing, so winning feels hollow.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Players repeatedly forgot that roles are redealt each round and used earlier claims as evidence. A reminder on screen at round start would help. The Wink also gives no signal beyond the death, so a lone Meowfia is hard to pin down.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Alex (would change): Make it clearer whether a player's reported role and visits are checkable against egg changes, and show each player's nest change per night more explicitly.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Blair (would change): I would make the dawn reports include who visited you when a role's egg gain depends on visitors, so the day debates would rest on facts rather than inference.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Casey (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so that claims can be checked without the table going around in circles.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make visit-count reports clearer, stating whether the visitor list includes the player's own visit, so people don't get tripped up.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Finley (would change): Show each player's role claim and night result in a single shared record so Meowfia lies are easier to catch.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Finley, round 3: Used round 1 and 2 claims as evidence about current roles. Also said Blair's 'role change' wasn't how the game works.
items.title: Drew Takes the Fall

items.text: Round 2 had one Meowfia who did almost nothing and won when Farm eggsecuted a Farm player. Fix: make a lone-Meowfia round harder to win, or give Meowfia some role in it.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs

items.text: Round 3 had no contradictions and no real leads, so Farm threw at a player with no basis. Fix: give Farm more info roles, or reward a Farm abstention.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs

items.text: Scoring snowballs: Casey led from round 1 and Ellis and Finley were out of the running early. Fix: a catch-up bonus or a cap on banked high cards.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs

items.text: Blair (would change): Make the dawn report clearer about what an animal learned versus what it gained, so players don't misread their own egg counts. Also state when a Wink lands in the day order so it's easier to plan.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs

items.text: Drew (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about which visits caused which egg changes, so players don't have to reconstruct the night from counts alone.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since several players built whole claims on guesses about their visitors.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make egg-gain rules visible in the dawn report, such as which visitor or role caused each gain, so players can check claims without reverse-engineering the payouts.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs

items.text: Rule arguments crowded out deduction. Most of the day went on what the rules say, not who lied. Fix: add a short rules recap or card text on each player's screen.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Rounds 1 and 2 had a lone Meowfia and almost no usable evidence, so Farm threw at the loudest accusation. The odds of 1 Meowfia seem too hard on Farm.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Speech turns were repetitive: players restated claims and asked 'who visited me?' repeatedly. Fewer beats or a tighter cap would cut the filler.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make the role texts clearer about whose nest an egg lands in, and state whether a Confused player's report is wrong in a way they can detect.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Blair (would change): Make the rules text for each animal unambiguous about whose nest receives an egg, so players aren't arguing about wording.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Casey (would change): Publish each player's visit and target list at dawn, so claims about visits and egg changes can be checked instead of argued.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Drew (would change): Make dawn reports say exactly which visit produced each egg gain, so players can check each other's counts without arguing over rules.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about whose nest an egg lands in, so players stop arguing over the rules instead of the evidence.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Blair, round 1: Said no change to his nest meant 'no one lands on me with a visit that gains eggs', and muddled the visit explanation.
items.title: Typo Gives It Away

items.text: Early CAW CAW calls ended rounds 1 and 3 quickly. Meowfia had little time to bluff. Consider requiring all 4 beats or more callers.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Score runaway: Blair got 11 then 17 points. Banking high cards when Farm wins makes round 1 and 2 leaders hard to catch. Check the point swing against the first-place-only goal.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: In round 3 a Meowfia win came from Farm splitting votes between two targets, not from deduction. The rules for two Meowfia and ties favour a focused Meowfia bloc.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Alex (confused by): The vote math was hard to track, especially how a thrown card from a dead player still counts as a card in the pile but not as a vote. The consolation return rule was also easy to misread.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Alex (would change): Make the Storyteller's reports clearer about which claims are verifiable, so players can tell a real egg from an unverified story.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Casey (would change): I would make role claims harder to fake, perhaps by giving each player a verifiable egg trail, so one convenient nest change can't back up a false story.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make egg changes clearer, for example by showing each dawn egg change publicly, so players can check claims without guessing.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Ellis (would change): Show each player's team as a public fact when a Meowfia player dies or wins, so the table can tell who has a partner left.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Drew, round 3: Threw only one card at Casey while Meowfia piled on Alex.
items.title: The Wink Flips It

items.text: Farm lost every round: the pile-on dynamic makes the day a rush to a consensus target by beat 3, with CAW CAW ending it before real questions. Consider requiring 4 CAWs or a minimum beat count.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: The Meowfia don't coordinate, but the one Meowfia player (Drew, Casey) just agreed with the table and won; with 1 Meowfia, lying has little cost. Score incentives for being the hidden Meowfia are strong.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Scores diverge oddly: the winner (Ellis) scored mostly from round 2, and Blair finished with 2 points after two Farm rounds ended with thrown cards lost. Throwing high cards at the consensus target is almost never costly, so throw size gave little signal.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Alex (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about who was confused and what was actually learned, so players don't have to guess which claims to trust.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make the dawn report say which information is unreliable, so confused players know which of their own claims to doubt.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Casey (would change): Make role claims and dawn reports easier to verify, such as showing each visit's source, so players aren't left guessing about confused reports.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Drew (confused by): Roles and alignments are redealt every round, so players who claimed different animals looked like liars when they were honest. Blair's repeated unexplained 2-egg losses were never resolved.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Drew (would change): Make the dawn reports easier to cross-check, such as showing who visited whom, so that unexplained egg losses like Blair's can actually be traced.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Ellis (would change): Make it clearer which claims are verifiable, such as a visit that leaves a visible mark in the dawn report, so players can check each other instead of relying on bluffs.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make dawn reports or the day listing clearer about who visited whom, so claims can be checked without guessing whether a player is confused.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Alex, round 2: Said Drew's 'not confused' report was the lie, though Drew had no reason to be confused if hugged.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Finley, round 3: Said Drew copied Casey's claim after Casey spoke, though Drew's claim was equally likely first in any order; also treated past-round claims as a tell.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Ellis, round 2: Seemingly believed Casey's 'nobody visited me' while knowing Ellis visited Casey; fine as a lie cover, but Ellis did not point out Casey's claim was false and the table never noticed.
items.title: Three Farm Funerals

items.text: Only one Meowfia in round 3 meant no teammate to check or bluff against. A false contradiction decided the round, and a single quiet Meowfia was almost untouchable.
items.title: Eagle Rules Meltdown

items.text: Round 1 and 2 votes ended fast on one nest-count mismatch, so little real deduction or bluffing was needed. Consider requiring more beats before CAW.
items.title: Eagle Rules Meltdown

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make the day's nest-change reports include who visited whom, so visitor claims could be checked without relying on memory.
items.title: Eagle Rules Meltdown

items.text: Casey (would change): Make dawn reports list visitors by animal so players can cross-check claims directly instead of arguing over who gained what.
items.title: Eagle Rules Meltdown

items.text: Ellis (would change): I would have dawn reports name each visitor when an egg is gained, so players could check claims against each other instead of arguing from counts.
items.title: Eagle Rules Meltdown

items.text: The consolation rule and the 13-value banking make a pile-on on a wrongly accused player pay off. Finley's one throw was worth 13 points, so Meowfia lying low is far better than any bluff.
items.title: The Eagle Rule Fiasco

items.text: Players can't verify claims, so bad rule readings decide votes. Consider letting the Storyteller post a short rules reminder or a confirmed fact each day.
items.title: The Eagle Rule Fiasco

items.text: Casey (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players aren't forced to reconstruct visit chains from egg counts alone.
items.title: The Eagle Rule Fiasco

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make the dawn report clearer about confusion, so a confused player's count is not mistaken for a lie by everyone else.
items.title: The Eagle Rule Fiasco

items.text: Alex, round 1: Explained his +0 muddily, and then said Casey's visit would mean he was visited, which is wrong as a rule reading.
items.title: The Eagle Rule Fiasco

items.text: Votes pile onto one player very early, since three CAWs end the day by beat 3. Players rarely test a second suspect. Consider needing all but one player to call, or a minimum number of beats.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Both Farm eggsecutions came from rule misunderstanding, not clever play. Meowfia won two rounds without doing much. Role text clarity matters more than balance here.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Scoring is lopsided. Round 3 gave Finley 9 points for one throw, deciding the game. Winners who throw a high card gain too much, while losers get almost nothing. Consider capping banked value.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Blair (would change): I would make dawn reports name the target and visitors more clearly, so players can check claims without guessing the rules.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about which visits and animals feed into each nest, so players can check claims faster.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Ellis (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since the day turned on players misreading their own egg changes.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Finley (would change): Show each player which animals visited them, not just the count, so the day debates rest on facts instead of reconstructed stories.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Alex, round 2: Claimed they visited Drew, then said they misspoke. Drew's lack of confusion exposed it.
items.title: The Eagle Nobody Believed

items.text: Voting is too cheap for Meowfia: throwing Wilds cost them nothing and no points were scored in round 1. Consider making throws cost something.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Turkeys

items.text: Dead players scoring full value (Drew banked 12 and then lost nothing) gives the winked player a big bonus. Consider capping dead players' points, or have the Wink also confiscate a throw.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Turkeys

items.text: Alex (would change): I'd make dawn reports clearer about whether an odd egg count is your own error or someone else's lie, so players don't have to guess.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Turkeys

items.text: Drew (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players aren't guessing at the rules and claims.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Turkeys

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make the dawn reports name the visitor's role when a role is revealed, so players can check claims against each other more easily.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Turkeys

items.text: Casey, round 1: Treated Alex's confused egg count as a real inconsistency.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Turkeys

items.text: Hugs are silent, which drove several bad arguments (rounds 2 and 3) about whether Ellis should have felt a hug. State plainly in the rules whether hugs are reported.
items.title: Hugs and Silent Winks

items.text: The score race is lopsided: Ellis's 8-point bank in round 1 decided the game, and later rounds barely threatened him. Add catch-up, or cap banked card value.
items.title: Hugs and Silent Winks

items.text: Players mostly threw Wilds and low cards at the Farm consensus, so the vote carried little risk. The throw-and-bank incentive rarely made anyone choose between teammates and their own score.
items.title: Hugs and Silent Winks

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since hugs and confusion made it hard to separate lies from honest mistakes. Each nest change should also be easier to trace back to a specific visit.
items.title: Hugs and Silent Winks

items.text: Casey (confused by): Whether dead players' throws still count, and how the Meowfia team's throws work when a teammate is one of the targets. I wasn't sure whether throwing at a teammate could ever help, so I didn't know how to weigh it.
items.title: Hugs and Silent Winks

items.text: Casey (would change): I'd make it clearer when a Wink is used and who it hits, since a dead player's vote was a surprise to me. I'd also show each player's role-group more openly so the Meowfia can coordinate.
items.title: Hugs and Silent Winks

items.text: Scores snowball. After round 1 Casey and Ellis led, and Alex was far behind, so Alex had no way back to first. Add a catch-up mechanism or reduce banking value.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: The rules do not say how ties for first are resolved. Casey and Ellis both finished with 18.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: Alex (would change): Make the dawn reports state exactly who visited whom, so players can check each claim against nest counts instead of arguing over ambiguous egg changes.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: Blair (would change): I would make the dawn reports name the visitor count and egg source more explicitly, so players can check claims without reconstructing every night.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make egg counts and visit claims easier to verify, perhaps by having the Storyteller publish each player's exact egg change at dawn.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make dawn reports say clearly when a player was confused and which parts might be wrong, so nobody has to guess.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: Ellis, round 2: Opened by saying her seat was gone and that she was a replacement, then had to correct herself.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: Casey, round 3: Treated a confirmed visit as proof Blair was clean, but a Meowfia can match a visit story with a cat teammate.
items.title: Winks and Wrong Owls

items.text: Players used roles from past rounds as evidence against Drew, even though roles are re-dealt every round. The rules should say this more plainly, or the day prompt should remind players. This drove two wrong eggsecutions.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Mob dynamics dominate. Once two or three players lean toward a target, everyone follows within one beat, and the CAW rule makes this faster. Consider requiring a stronger quorum or fewer early CAWs.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: The scoring leans heavily on the leader. Drew started with a big nest, and a lost round gives the other team's winners almost nothing (Blair won with 0 points in round 2). Winning cheaply with Wilds pays little. Consider a flat bonus for winning.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make the dawn report clearer about when a player is confused, so that a confused player knows which part of their information to distrust.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Casey (would change): Let the dawn report name the visiting role when it reveals a visitor, so claims about who visited whom could be checked against each other directly.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the dawn reports show which visits went to whom, so claims could be checked against the actual chain instead of counts alone.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Finley (confused by): The Wink was confusing because Casey collapsed and I couldn't tell whether the Storyteller had revealed my Wink or just the outcome. The rules for a Meowfia player who lost their Wink target were also unclear.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Finley (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about which visits and egg changes came from which role, so that claims are easier to cross-check.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Finley, round 1: Said Drew's visitor list was wrong, as if Drew had claimed visitors to himself. Finley retracted it later.
items.title: Wrong Cat, Right Mob

items.text: Round 1 had only one Meowfia and no real cover for the table to examine. Five players threw at a Farm player over a rules quibble, so a round can go wrong from rules debate alone.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: Most throws were Wilds or one low card, so the bank-or-keep decision barely mattered. Scores moved little, and a bigger reward for correct throws would sharpen risk.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make dawn reports name the source of every egg gained, so players can verify claims without guessing.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make the dawn report say clearly whether a visit was received, so confused players can check their own nest changes against the rules.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: Casey (would change): I would make dawn reports state clearly when a visit caused confusion and what the source of each egg was, so claims are easier to verify.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since several claims depended on counts nobody could verify. Clearer visit information would make the day less of a guessing game.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: Finley (would change): Tell confused players' dawn reports apart from clean ones more clearly, so the table can weigh them properly.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: Ellis, round 2: Said Casey visited Blair, so Blair might be confused. He treated Casey's claim as true while the table was testing it.
items.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair

items.text: The Wink is too strong. Drew winked in the middle of the day, silenced a truthful Farm player, and took 16 points in a single round. Consider a cost or a limited effect.
items.title: Turkey Rule Confusion

items.text: Scoring snowballs. One round of 16 points for a King-heavy throw decided the whole game. Drew led 22 to 11 after round 2, which made round 3 irrelevant. Add a catch-up rule or cap the value of banked cards.
items.title: Turkey Rule Confusion

items.text: Many players just agreed with the first accusation. Round 1 and round 3 each saw a near-unanimous throw by the third beat, so players with a hidden role had little to decide.
items.title: Turkey Rule Confusion

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make the role claims and visit results easier to cross-check, such as showing each player's visit targets on the dawn report. Several rounds turned on who was lying about a visit, and the table had no clean way to verify it.
items.title: Turkey Rule Confusion

items.text: Drew (would change): I'd make the day's role claims and visit results easier to verify, perhaps by having the Storyteller confirm each player's visit outcome publicly.
items.title: Turkey Rule Confusion

items.text: Ellis (would change): Put the death status and the round number in each dawn or day report so players don't carry over a dead role from the previous round.
items.title: Turkey Rule Confusion

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make the visit and role information clearer, so a visit that gains or loses an egg is easier to trace back to its source.
items.title: Turkey Rule Confusion

items.text: Finley's round-1 10-point throw decided the game. A strong early lead with no catch-up mechanism made rounds 2 and 3 low in tension. Cap how much a single throw can bank, or add a comeback pull.
items.title: Ellis Takes the Fall

items.text: Everyone converged on one target each round. Few players built a competing story, so the votes felt like a pile-on, not a debate.
items.title: Ellis Takes the Fall

items.text: Confusion and hugging hid information in round 3, and the +1 in Drew's nest had no clean explanation. The table threw at a Farm player on thin evidence. Give confused players a way to be cleared, or reveal nest changes at dawn more clearly.
items.title: Ellis Takes the Fall

items.text: Alex (would change): I would make dawn reports say exactly who visited you, so the table stops building theories on partial information.
items.title: Ellis Takes the Fall

items.text: Blair (would change): Have the dawn reports state the source of each egg change, so players can check claims without guessing.
items.title: Ellis Takes the Fall

items.text: Casey (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who gained or lost eggs and why, so players can check claims without guessing.

items.text: A lone Meowfia winning round 3 banked 34 points. Banking cards at full value lets one round decide the whole game. Consider capping banked value per round or scaling it by team size.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Players often repeated each other's reads and asked questions already answered. Beats felt samey, with several 'nothing new to add' turns.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Wilds make early throws almost free, so Farm piled on cheaply in rounds 1 and 2. The score hinges on a few high cards, which makes most votes feel low-stakes.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Blair (would change): I'd make the dawn report state which parts are confused, since "this report may be wrong" gave no way to check the egg or the role.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Casey (confused by): The vote math was hard to track: Drew's 5-card throw at Alex swung round 3, and I couldn't tell how many cards each side would bank or lose. Throw counts versus card values stayed unclear to me.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Drew (would change): I would make the dawn reports clearer about which visits actually caused egg changes, so players can check claims against each other without guessing.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Ellis (would change): I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which visits and eggs are confirmed versus claimed, so players don't have to guess from a confused report.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Finley (would change): I'd make confused reports easier to trace, such as saying whether the egg source is known, so the table isn't left guessing whether a gain is real.
items.title: The Quiet Mouser

items.text: Round 1 had effectively no deduction. Most roles gave nothing, so the table picked the one player with a confused report. A fix is to make sure each round has at least some usable hard evidence.
items.title: Floofer Gets Caught

items.text: Meowfia throwing at Farm players barely mattered, and the Wink did nothing in round 2. Killing a caller removed no vote that mattered, so Alex still lost. Consider letting a Wink also block that player's throw, or make the dead player's votes drop.
items.title: Floofer Gets Caught

items.text: Voting piles on one player almost unanimously every round, with single low-card throws. The scoring gives little reason to bet big, so the Eggsecution lacked tension. Consider rewarding higher throws more.
items.title: Floofer Gets Caught

items.text: Ellis won with 12 points largely from one round-three 5 banked, while playing quietly as Meowfia in round 2. Second-place-is-a-loss plus silence rewards hiding, so the quiet cat was never targeted. Consider a nudge for the silent.

items.text: Finley (would change): Make the dawn reports clearer about which visits were confirmed versus confused, so players can cross-check claims without guessing.
